Hi Priya and Karthik,

Thanks for the clear note and attachments — helpful. Short answer: in several EU/US VAT regimes our billing engine calculates tax on the gross taxable supply (the usage) and posts the promotional credit as a separate line item. That can make it look like tax was assessed on the full amount. Practically speaking, the net customer liability should be zero when a promotional credit covers the taxable base, but our invoice system historically shows tax on the gross line and then a negative credit line, which leaves the tax line visible.

What we'll do for Acme Corp:
- We'll generate a credit memo that offsets the invoice tax (draft attached as draft-credit-memo-ACME.pdf).
- We'll issue a corrected invoice that references the credit memo so your AP team sees a zero net due.
- Timeline: credit memo + corrected invoice within 3 business days once we confirm Acme's billing profile (VAT reg. number).

Action items for Acme (please reply to this thread or upload to the Drive link):
- If you have a VAT registration number or reseller exemption certificate, send it to acme-billing@acmecorp.com (or drop in the Drive link).

Notes / reasoning for your finance team:
- Tax is calculated on taxable charge amount; promo credits reduce the net amount due but in many jurisdictions the tax authority expects the taxable transaction to be recorded and then a credit applied, rather than suppressing the tax line entirely.
- The credit memo will make your internal ledger match (tax liability removed / credit recorded).

Let me know if you prefer we escalate to our tax counsel for a formal note, otherwise I'll proceed to issue the credit memo and corrected invoice on receipt of any VAT docs.

Best,
